confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches. These returned crowdsourced and travel-budget price guides that differ in date, currency and whether they cover Interlaken or nearby towns. Searches turned up CHF 4-5 for a cappuccino, about CHF 7-9 for a 0.5L draft beer, about $31 (CHF 25) for a cheap meal, and about $99 for a mid-range meal for two. I raised the mid-range figure to reflect tourist-season pricing and my own CHF-to-USD conversion at about 1.25 USD per CHF. Only one source gave a cocktail price ($12-15), which looked low for Switzerland, so I set cocktail from the local beer relationship and general Swiss knowledge. Wine by the glass is based on sources giving about CHF 7-12. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season from general knowledge; I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. They are the least certain anchors, because July prices in Interlaken swing widely with demand. The FX search result was a summary of the RBA exchange-rate page showing 0.6720 for 2026-11-18. I did not open the page myself, and the same search also returned older cached snapshots with different rates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Swiss Alpine tourist towns such as Lucerne, Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen. Interlaken prices are high for Switzerland and well above the typical European average.
